cookie-bar-with-chocolate-nuts-and-graha.title: Cookie Bar with Chocolate, Nuts and Graham Crackers

content.title: About
content.content: The cookie bar combines crunchy graham crackers, rich milk chocolate, and a blend of toasted nuts. It is designed for fans of sweet‑nutty flavors, offering a balanced texture: soft inside with a crisp exterior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Graham crackers originated in the United States in the late 19th century and are a base for many desserts.
The chocolate coating is thin enough to keep the nuts crunchy.
The nut mix usually includes walnuts, hazelnuts and almonds, boosting the content of healthy fats.
The bar is packaged in single‑serve portions, making it popular for office snacks.
When stored properly, the product stays fresh for up to 6 months.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Chocolate provides flavonoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Nuts supply monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Graham crackers and nuts are high in fiber, promoting normal digestion.

items.title: Energy sustaining
items.content: The combination of carbs from the crackers and fats from the nuts offers lasting satiety and energy.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The bar provides magnesium, iron, vitamin E and B‑complex vitamins important for metabolic processes.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: The product contains nuts, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The bar is calorie‑dense, so moderate portion sizes are recommended.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The chocolate layer adds sugar, which may be a concern for people with diabetes or low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Chocolate contains a small amount of caffeine, which should be considered by caffeine‑sensitive persons.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bar as a standalone snack, break it into pieces and add to yogurt, ice cream or a salad. It can be lightly warmed in the microwave to melt the chocolate for a gooier texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bar in an airtight package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer storage, refrigerate to prevent the chocolate from blooming.

content.title: About
content.content: Corn nuts are roasted whole corn kernels that become crunchy and lightly salted after processing. They have a distinctive roasted‑corn aroma and a dense texture that resembles nuts, although botanically they are not nuts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn nuts were introduced in the United States in the 1930s as a cinema snack.
To achieve their crunch, the kernels are first soaked and then deep‑fried at high temperature.
Several flavor variants exist: classic salted, barbecue, cheese, spicy chili, and more.
The corn used is often a small‑kernel variety (similar to popcorn), but the grains are dried and fried rather than popped.
In some countries they are called “roasted corn” or “corn chips shaped like nuts.”

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Corn nuts provide fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Corn contains carotenoids and phenolic compounds with antioxidant activity.

items.title: Low sodium (unsalted version)
items.content: Unsalted corn nuts can be a better alternative to heavily salted snacks.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: The carbohydrates in corn are rapidly digestible, making the snack convenient for active people.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Corn is naturally gluten‑free, so corn nuts are suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salted varieties can contain a lot of sodium, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Corn nuts are relatively calorie‑dense, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: The hard texture can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn nuts can be enjoyed straight from the bag, added to salads, soups, or used as a crunchy topping for yogurts and porridge. They are also commonly served with dips such as cheese or spicy sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep corn nuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.

fish-white-mixed-species-baked-or-broile.title: White fish, mixed species, baked or broiled

content.title: About
content.content: White fish, mixed species, baked or broiled is a ready‑to‑eat product made from a blend of white fish varieties (cod, pollock, hake, etc.) that have been thermally processed by baking or broiling. It offers a mild flavor, tender texture, and is convenient for quick meal preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A blend of white fish provides a more consistent taste and texture than a single species.
Baking retains more nutrients, while broiling creates a crispier exterior.
White fish generally contains less fat than red fish, making it popular among calorie‑conscious eaters.
The product is often used in children’s meals and diet menus because of its mild flavor.
Thermal processing eliminates most pathogenic bacteria, allowing for extended shelf life.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: White fish supplies high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Its low fat content helps maintain a healthy calorie balance.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Even lean white fish provides beneficial omega‑3s that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It is a good source of B12, B6, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The product provides selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, vital for thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Certain fish can contain trace amounts of mercury, though levels in mixed white fish are typically low.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: The ready‑made product often contains added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to eat: heat in the microwave or oven, add to salads, pastas, soups, or use as a sandwich filling. It pairs well with lemon, herbs, and light sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in the original packaging for up to 5 days after opening. Freeze at –18 °C for longer storage (up to 3 months).

fruit-flavored-drink-with-high-vitamin-c.title: Fruit Flavored Drink, Powdered, High in Vitamin C, Ready-to-Reconstitute

content.title: About
content.content: A powdered fruit drink with a high vitamin C content designed for quick preparation: just add water and you get a refreshing beverage with a bright fruit flavor. The vitamin C provides immune support and antioxidant protection.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The powdered form allows long‑term storage without loss of taste or nutritional value.
Vitamin C is stabilized with special antioxidants, preserving its activity even after extended shelf life.
The fruit aroma is derived from natural extracts rather than artificial flavorings.
Each serving supplies more than 100 % of the adult daily value for vitamin C.
The product is easy to transport and ideal for camping, work, or travel.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C enhances immune‑cell function, helping the body fight infections.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Vitamin C neutralizes free radicals, reducing oxidative stress in cells.

items.title: Improved iron absorption
items.content: Vitamin C increases the bioavailability of iron from plant foods, beneficial for anemia.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The drink helps replenish body fluids, especially in hot weather or after exercise.

items.title: Skin health
items.content: Vitamin C participates in collagen synthesis, supporting skin elasticity and appearance.

items.title: Allergy to fruit extracts
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the flavoring components.

items.title: Excessive vitamin C intake
items.content: Very high doses can cause gastrointestinal discomfort such as diarrhea.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Vitamin C may affect the efficacy of certain drugs, for example anticoagulants.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Mix one serving (approximately 10 g) with 250 ml of cold water, stir until fully dissolved. Optionally add ice or fresh fruit pieces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the package tightly sealed to prevent moisture. See the package for the expiration date.

content.title: About
content.content: Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus) is an edible pod widely used in cooking. The frozen, cooked version with added fat is designed for quick meal preparation, retaining the vegetable’s characteristic tender taste and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Okra is known as "lady’s finger", "gumbo" and "bhindi" in different regions.
Its mucilaginous content makes it popular for thickening soups, stews and gumbos.
In the United States okra is classified as a vegetable, while in some Asian countries it is considered a fruit.
Freezing preserves most B‑vitamins and carotenoids, though some vitamin C is lost during cooking.
Okra is used in traditional medicine to support digestion.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber helps regulate bowel movements and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Okra provides about 30 kcal per 100 g, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of vitamins A and C
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, while vitamin C contributes to immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Potassium, magnesium and iron aid blood pressure regulation and muscle function.

items.title: Mucilaginous compounds
items.content: The slime has mild anti‑inflammatory properties and may soothe gastritis symptoms.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to okra, ranging from skin rash to swelling.

items.title: Mucilage sensitivity
items.content: Large amounts of mucilage can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Okra contains oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in predisposed individuals.

items.title: Added fat
items.content: The added fat increases the product’s calorie content; those monitoring fat intake should account for it.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: After thawing, add the pods to soups, stews, curries, pasta dishes and vegetable casseroles. The fat makes the dish richer, so it works well for sautéing and braising. Okra pairs nicely with tomatoes, garlic, onion and spices such as cumin and paprika.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen okra in its original packaging at –18 °C. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. Do not refreeze.

rice-white-with-carrots-dark-green-veget.title: White Rice with Carrots, Dark Green Vegetables and Tomato‑Based Sauce, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of boiled white rice, sliced carrots, dark green vegetables (such as broccoli or spinach) and tomato sauce or fresh tomatoes. No fat is added, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is one of the most widely consumed grains worldwide.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Dark green vegetables contain chlorophyll and high amounts of vitamin K.
Tomato sauce provides lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
The dish’s lack of added fat preserves the natural taste of the ingredients.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice supplies quick‑digesting carbohydrates that fuel the body.

items.title: Eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots and lycopene from tomatoes support visual health.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Dark green vegetables are rich in vitamin K and calcium, important for strong bones.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene and chlorophyll help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: The absence of added fat makes the meal suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or tomato sauce.

items.title: Low fiber
items.content: Compared with whole‑grain rice, white rice provides less dietary fiber.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish as a side to meat, fish or legumes. It also works well in lunch boxes. If desired, add spices such as turmeric or paprika without using oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared meal in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat using a microwave or steam to avoid drying out.
